stem: Which substance is required by coenzymes in the process described?
rationale: The process is aerobic and requires oxygen as the final oxidant of the reduced coenzymes. The enzymes of the citric acid cycle are located in the mitochondrial matrix.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE PROVIDES SUBSTRATES FOR THE RESPIRATORY CHAIN

stem: Which substrate does citrate synthase act on?
rationale: The initial reaction between acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate to form citrate is catalyzed by citrate synthase.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: What substance is citryl-CoA converted into?
rationale: The thioester bond of the resultant citryl-CoA is hydrolyzed, releasing citrate and CoASH.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: Which substrate does aconitase act on?
rationale: Citrate is isomerized to isocitrate by the enzyme aconitase.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: Which substance is required by citrate in the described process?
rationale: Channeling ensures that citrate is only available in free solution when aconitase is inhibited by isocitrate accumulation.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: What substance is succinyl-CoA converted into?
rationale: The reaction involves the transfer of CoA from succinyl-CoA to acetoacetate. The transfer of CoA results in the formation of acetoacetyl-CoA and succinate.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: Which substrate does succinate thiokinase act on?
rationale: Succinyl-CoA is converted to succinate by the enzyme succinate thiokinase (succinyl-CoA synthetase). Succinyl-CoA is the only example of substrate-level phosphorylation in the citric acid cycle.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: Which substrate does succinate dehydrogenase act on?
rationale: The first dehydrogenation reaction, forming fumarate, is catalyzed by succinate dehydrogenase.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: What substance is NADH converted into?
rationale: NADH is reoxidized to NAD by the respiratory chain.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: What substance is oxaloacetate converted into?
rationale: During gluconeogenesis, some of the label in oxaloacetate is incorporated into glucose and glycogen.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > REACTIONS OF THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE GENERATE REDUCING EQUIVALENTS & CO₂

stem: In the citric acid cycle, FAD acts on which substrate?
rationale: Riboflavin is essential in the citric acid cycle as FAD, the cofactor for succinate dehydrogenase.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > VITAMINS PLAY KEY ROLES IN THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE

stem: Pantothenic acid is converted into which substance?
rationale: Pantothenic acid is part of coenzyme A, which is esterified to carboxylic acids to form acetyl-CoA and succinyl-CoA.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > VITAMINS PLAY KEY ROLES IN THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE

stem: Which substance is synthesized by succinate thiokinase?
rationale: The GTP required for this reaction is provided by the GDP-dependent isoenzyme of succinate thiokinase.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE PLAYS A PIVOTAL ROLE IN METABOLISM > The Citric Acid Cycle Takes Part in Gluconeogenesis, Transamination, & Deamination

stem: Oxaloacetate is found within which structure?
rationale: Oxaloacetate leads to the production of glucose in the liver and kidney.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE PLAYS A PIVOTAL ROLE IN METABOLISM > The Citric Acid Cycle Takes Part in Gluconeogenesis, Transamination, & Deamination

stem: Pyruvate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Pyruvate can then undergo oxidative decarboxylation to acetyl-CoA by pyruvate dehydrogenase.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE PLAYS A PIVOTAL ROLE IN METABOLISM > The Citric Acid Cycle Takes Part in Gluconeogenesis, Transamination, & Deamination

stem: Propionyl CoA is converted into which substance?
rationale: Various compounds can yield propionyl CoA, which can be carboxylated and isomerized to succinyl CoA, making them important anaplerotic substrates.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE PLAYS A PIVOTAL ROLE IN METABOLISM > The Citric Acid Cycle Takes Part in Gluconeogenesis, Transamination, & Deamination

stem: Phosphoenolpyruvate is converted into which substance?
rationale: Phosphoenolpyruvate is then dephosphorylated to form pyruvate by pyruvate kinase.
citation: chapter_16_the_citric_acid_cycle_a_pathway_central_to_carbohydrate_lipid_and_amino_acid_metabolism — Overview > THE CITRIC ACID CYCLE PLAYS A PIVOTAL ROLE IN METABOLISM > The Citric Acid Cycle Takes Part in Gluconeogenesis, Transamination, & Deamination
